stories.headline: Canada's retaliation tests the limit of American power under Trump
stories.summary: Canada has imposed retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on American goods in response to Trump administration trade measures, matching the scope of US actions against Canadian imports. The escalation tests whether traditional economic leverage remains effective as both countries signal willingness to sustain a prolonged trade conflict.

stories.headline: From 'dirt poor' to philanthropic superstar - the life of Dolly Parton
stories.summary: Dolly Parton, who rose from poverty in rural Tennessee to become one of country music's most influential figures, has died at age 80. Throughout her seven-decade career, she earned widespread respect across political and cultural divides through her music, business ventures, and philanthropic work, including her Imagination Library that has distributed millions of books to children worldwide.

stories.headline: At least 14 babies killed in Pakistan hospital nursery fire
stories.summary: A fire broke out in the nursery ward of a hospital in Pakistan's capital, killing at least 14 newborns and prompting immediate investigation by officials. The blaze appears to have been triggered by an air-conditioning unit malfunction, raising questions about safety protocols in the maternity facility.

stories.headline: At least 17 killed as flash flood sweeps part of Nepal-Tibet border
stories.summary: A flash flood has struck the Nepal-Tibet border region, killing at least 17 people and destroying villages and infrastructure across the area. The disaster has damaged roads and energy facilities, with search efforts ongoing for those reported missing in the affected communities.

stories.headline: Haiti gang raid death toll rises to 47 as more than 50 kidnapped, says UN
stories.summary: A gang attack near Haiti's capital killed at least 47 people and resulted in more than 50 kidnappings, according to UN reports. The violence reflects the escalating gang activity that has destabilized the country's security situation in recent months.

stories.headline: Lindsey Graham’s sister up for election to his US Senate seat
stories.summary: Darline Graham, the sister of late Senator Lindsey Graham, wins the South Carolina Republican nomination to fill his vacant Senate seat. Trump's endorsement proves decisive in her victory, though she faces scrutiny over her foreign policy positions ahead of the general election.

stories.headline: CIA chief travels to Moscow for unannounced talks, US media reports
stories.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe has made an unannounced visit to Moscow to meet with Russian intelligence officials, marking a rare direct engagement between the agencies. The Kremlin confirmed the talks occurred, suggesting a potential channel for communication between the US and Russia on matters of mutual concern.

stories.headline: Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles
stories.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams reached the quarterfinal of the US Open mixed doubles tournament before losing their match. Their pairing generated significant fan interest as two of tennis's most prominent players competed together in a rarely-played format.

stories.headline: The RSF’s defeat will not end Sudan’s war but merely fragment it
stories.summary: Sudan's conflict will persist even if the RSF military faction faces military defeat, as the underlying political divisions and fragmentation among armed groups create conditions for prolonged instability rather than resolution. Regional tensions with Chad and Ethiopia, combined with international divisions over arms embargoes, suggest the war's reach and consequences extend beyond Sudan's borders while diplomatic pathways remain blocked.

stories.headline: US immigration agents arrested more than 49,500 people in July
stories.summary: US immigration enforcement agents arrested more than 49,500 people in July, marking the highest monthly total since the current administration's deportation initiatives began. The surge reflects intensified enforcement operations across the country targeting undocumented immigrants.
